translationRepairs: When the Kazakh khan Abulai refused to fight, they routed him, took more than a hundred heads, and seized over two hundred horses.
When the Kazakh khan Abulai gave battle, they defeated him, took more than a hundred heads, and seized over two hundred horses.
s0007 has 拒戰 followed by 擊敗之: Abulai offered resistance in battle and was defeated. “Refused to fight” contradicts the engagement that yielded more than a hundred heads.
The Kazakh khan Abulai refused battle; they defeated him, beheaded more than a hundred men, and captured more than two hundred horses.
The Kazakh khan Abulai resisted in battle; they defeated him, beheaded more than a hundred men, and captured more than two hundred horses.
The literal likewise turns 拒戰 into refusal of battle; “resisted in battle” matches 拒戰 and the following 擊敗之 without other changes.
By the time the army reached Barkul, Zhao Hui's siege had already been lifted, and they united with Fu De's army.
By the time the army reached Barcuk, Zhao Hui's siege had already been lifted, and they united with Fu De's army.
s0017 names 巴爾楚克 (Barcuk/Bachu). Barkul/Barkol is 巴里坤 elsewhere; the place of junction after relieving Zhao Hui must be Barcuk.
When the army reached Barkul, Zhao Hui's siege had already been lifted, and they joined Fu De's forces.
When the army reached Barcuk, Zhao Hui's siege had already been lifted, and they joined Fu De's forces.
The literal repeats Barkul for 巴爾楚克; Barcuk restores the correct toponym while leaving the rest of the sentence intact.

When the Dorbet taiji Boshigashi and Ubashi submitted, the emperor made Boshigashi a prince and Ubashi a beile, with pasture on the Irtysh; Shu Ming memorialized asking that they remain garrisoned at Hadaqingjile.

When the Dorbet taiji Boshigashi and Ubashi submitted, the emperor made Boshigashi a prince and Ubashi a beise, with pasture on the Irtysh; Shu Ming memorialized asking that they remain garrisoned at Hadaqingjile.
s0075 grants Ubashi 貝子 (beise). Beile is 貝勒, a different rank; the proposal correctly distinguishes the titles.

The Dorbet taiji Boshigashi and Ubashi submitted; the emperor made Boshigashi a prince and Ubashi a beile, with pasture on the Irtysh; Shu Ming memorialized asking that they remain garrisoned at Hadaqingjile.

The Dorbet taiji Boshigashi and Ubashi submitted; the emperor made Boshigashi a prince and Ubashi a beise, with pasture on the Irtysh; Shu Ming memorialized asking that they remain garrisoned at Hadaqingjile.
The literal also misrenders 貝子 as beile; beise is the standard English for 貝子 and matches the Chinese grant.
When the emperor heard that the Khoshut Chinggunjab was about to rebel, he ordered Shu Ming to investigate.
When the emperor heard that the Khotogoid Chinggunjab was about to rebel, he ordered Shu Ming to investigate.
s0079 identifies Chinggunjab as 和托輝特 (Khotogoid). Khoshut would be 和碩特; the proposal corrects the tribal affiliation.
The emperor heard that the Khoshut Chinggunjab was about to rebel and ordered Shu Ming to reconnoiter.
The emperor heard that the Khotogoid Chinggunjab was about to rebel and ordered Shu Ming to reconnoiter.
The literal repeats Khoshut for 和托輝特; Khotogoid restores the correct ethnonym without altering the rest.
His younger brother Ba Ling'a, from imperial guards corporal was promoted in succession to second-class bodyguard and appointed Chahar commander.
His younger brother Ba Ling'a rose from imperial guards corporal through successive promotions to second-class bodyguard and was appointed Chahar commander.
The literal before is ungrammatical (“from imperial guards corporal was promoted…”). The replacement preserves 自親軍校累遷二等侍衛，授察哈爾總管 in fluent English.

They set up courier stations from Barkul to Jierhalang and pursued bandits at Shalabohuoshi Ridge; they met the Dorbet Namuchi at pasture, who begged to surrender but soon fled; Ai Long'a caught up with him, killed more than a thousand men, and Namuchi then submitted.

They set up courier stations from Barcuk to Jierhalang and pursued bandits at Shalabohuoshi Ridge; they met the Dorbet Namuchi at pasture, who begged to surrender but soon fled; Ai Long'a caught up with him, killed more than a thousand men, and Namuchi then submitted.
s0039 has 巴爾楚克, not 巴里坤. Barkul is wrong, but Barkol (巴里坤) is also wrong here; Barcuk matches the Chinese and the accepted reading of the same toponym in s0017.
With Vice Commandant Jifu and bodyguard De'ersenbao he went to the Khalkha Chakhar department to capture bandits and took several fugitives.
With Vice Commandant Jifu and bodyguard De'ersenbao he went to the Khalkha Setsen department to capture bandits and took several fugitives.
s0170 has 喀爾喀車臣部, the Khalkha Setsen Khan department. Chakhar is 察哈爾 and is a different polity.
Together with Vice Commandant Jifu and bodyguard De'ersenbao he went to the Khalkha Chakhar department to capture bandits and obtained fugitive bandits.
Together with Vice Commandant Jifu and bodyguard De'ersenbao he went to the Khalkha Setsen department to capture bandits and obtained fugitive bandits.
The literal repeats Chakhar for 車臣部; Setsen restores the correct Khalkha aimag name.
In the eleventh year of the Qianlong reign, Sichuan governor-general Qingfu campaigned against the lower Zang chief Banbo, and Nusan was ordered to join Qingfu's army.
In the eleventh year of the Qianlong reign, Sichuan governor-general Qingfu campaigned against the lower Zhandui chief Banbo, and Nusan was ordered to join Qingfu's army.
s0190 has 下瞻對頭人班滾. “Lower Zang” drops 瞻對; lower Zhandui recovers the full place-name.
In the eleventh year of Qianlong, Sichuan governor-general Qingfu campaigned against the lower Zang chief Banbo; Nusan was ordered to join Qingfu's army.
In the eleventh year of Qianlong, Sichuan governor-general Qingfu campaigned against the lower Zhandui chief Banbo; Nusan was ordered to join Qingfu's army.
The literal likewise omits 瞻對 by saying “lower Zang”; lower Zhandui matches 下瞻對.

Nusan and Wuleideng themselves stated that the matter of seizing livestock and concealing them for private gain had begun with Salai'er; the emperor held that Salai'er had only recently submitted and did not know the law, and rebuked Nusan and the others for not being allowed to shift blame onto him.

Nusan and Wuleideng themselves stated that the matter of seizing livestock and concealing them for private gain had begun with Salai'er; the emperor held that Salai'er had only recently submitted and did not know the law, and rebuked Nusan and the others for shifting the blame onto him.
責…不得以此諉過 rebukes them for shifting blame onto Salai’er. The old literal “for not being allowed to shift blame” reverses the force of the rebuke.
Soon after, for failing to capture Mahaqin effectively, he was ordered to serve in a supervisory capacity over the column commanders.
Soon after, for failing to capture Mahaqin effectively, he was ordered to serve in the capacity of a column commander.
在領隊大臣上行走 is the Qing formula for serving in the capacity of column commander, not supervising officers above that rank. The demotion after 捕瑪哈沁不力 fits an acting/column-commander posting.
Shortly thereafter, for ineffective pursuit of Mahaqin, he was ordered to serve above the column commanders.
Shortly thereafter, for ineffective pursuit of Mahaqin, he was ordered to serve in the capacity of column commander.
The literal “serve above the column commanders” misreads 上行走 as spatial “above”; “in the capacity of column commander” is the correct formula.
